domain: EU food-safety scientific assessment / EFSA health-claim opinion outcome prediction (claim-level regulatory-outcome task, EU agency + Commission publisher pair)

jurisdiction.publisher: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) for the claims corpus and opinions; Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety (DG SANTE, European Commission) for the EU Register of Nutrition and Health Claims

prediction_question: For a health claim submitted to EFSA under Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006 - either a general-function claim (Art. 13.1) from the Member State list, or an application (Art. 13.5 / Art. 14) received via a national competent authority - will EFSA's NDA Panel conclude that a cause-and-effect relationship is established (favourable opinion), rather than not established (unfavourable)?
prediction_time: For Art. 13.5/14 applications: the instant EFSA receives/validates the application (published per the Transparency Regulation regime on OpenEFSA); the Panel 'shall' adopt its opinion within 5 months excluding stop-the-clock periods (EFSA guidance). For the Art. 13.1 batch: the compilation of the Member State claim list (4,637 main entries, published as the EFSA claims database, 2010) precedes the Panel's wave evaluations (2009-2011). Features are the submitted claim content only: claim wording, food/constituent, claimed effect, target group, conditions of use, article route, applicant identity (13.5/14). NOT YET WORKED AS A DATED EXAMPLE - one OpenEFSA-record worked example (application receipt instant vs opinion adoption date, with the feature window in between) is a named open item below.
target_definition: Binary: favourable vs unfavourable Panel conclusion on the claim. Label source: the published EFSA Journal opinion's conclusion ('a cause and effect relationship has [not] been established'), cross-checkable against the Commission's EU Register of Nutrition and Health Claims (authorised vs non-authorised status + reasons). Label source columns are excludable from shipped features; the register/opinion fields that carry the outcome are not features.

sources.name: Commission EU Register of Nutrition and Health Claims (DG SANTE) via the Food and Feed Information Portal
sources.access: Searchable register now served by the FIP SPA (https://ec.europa.eu/food/food-feed-portal/screen/health-claims/eu-register). Backend API base found in the app's own env config (assets/env-json-config.json): https://ec.europa.eu/food/food-feed-portal/backend/api - MEASURED WORKING 2026-11-03 for e.g. /policy-items?foodDomain=nf&authorisationType=nf_auth and /food_categories?domain_code=nf (JSON 200). The health_claims endpoints present in the app bundle (/health_claims/get_list_of_claims, /health_claims/get_claim_details?claim_id=, /health_claims/get_list_of_individual_auth_claims) returned 404 from a plain HTTP client with the app's base config and browser-like headers; the SPA did not render its API calls in the supported browser either (page stayed in loading state). Per-claim structured outcome extraction is the named open item.

sources.name: EFSA Journal (NDA Panel scientific opinions)
sources.access: MEASURED 2026-11-03: pdfdirect and article URLs return 403 to plain HTTP clients (Wiley bot blocking); EFSA's own /en/efsajournal/pub/<id> routes 301-redirect to the Wiley host. Opinion conclusions are therefore NOT yet extractable from this host - unverified whether the supported browser passes Wiley's challenge. This is the main access risk, recorded as such.
sources.licence: EFSA website terms apply ('unless otherwise stated'); per-document copyright line not yet verified (blocked by the same 403).

license_evidence: EFSA legal notice (https://www.efsa.europa.eu/en/legalnotice, fetched directly 2026-11-03, HTTP 200): 'Copyright © for the entire content of this website unless otherwise stated: European Food Safety Authority – EFSA. Re-use is authorised, provided that EFSA is acknowledged as the source of the material.' No database-replication prohibition of the ECHA kind; per-document caveats ('unless otherwise stated', individual copyright notices) must be verified for the EFSA Journal PDFs before construction.

Commission legal notice (https://commission.europa.eu/legal-notice_en, fetched 2026-11-03, HTTP 200): 'Unless otherwise indicated (e.g. in individual copyright notices), content owned by the EU on this website is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence.' The EU Register of Nutrition and Health Claims is DG SANTE content (data.europa.eu dataset id u3yjqnr7wx2gjkbqmajsya, publisher corporate-body/SANTE).

Tentative classification: class B for the EFSA side (attribution + per-document verification still open on the Wiley-hosted journal PDFs), class A for the Commission register side. Not final: per-document notices unread, blocked by the Wiley 403.
split_strategy: Candidate (counts not yet measured from the source - the named gap): temporal split at opinion-adoption level, train = Art 13.1 batch opinions (2009-2011) + early Art 13.5/14 applications (2008-2015), eval = 2016-2020, holdout = 2021-2025. Positives cluster by opinion: one NDA Panel opinion can decide dozens of Art 13.1 claims at once, so claim rows within one opinion are NOT independent and the clustered (opinion-level) count must be recorded with the claim-level count. Published publisher statistics (cross-check evidence, not a measured panel): 2,758 general-function claims assessed by 28 July 2011 with 'about one in five' favourable (EFSA press news 110728); Art 13.5/14 applications finalised by Nov 2013: 91 (13 positive / 78 negative) and 100 (33 positive / 67 negative) (EFSA NDA presentation, document 131120-p03.pdf) - roughly 20-33% favourable depending on route.

measurements.access_measured: 2026-11-03, all anonymous plain HTTP from the coordinator: (1) ndaclaims13.zip -> 200, 8,341,996 bytes; (2) EFSA /en/legalnotice -> 200, terms quoted in license_evidence; (3) commission.europa.eu/legal-notice_en -> 200 (follows 301 from ec.europa.eu/info), CC BY 4.0 quoted; (4) efsa.onlinelibrary.wiley.com pdfdirect URL -> 403 to curl; (5) FIP backend /policy-items and /food_categories -> JSON 200, /health_claims/* -> 404 from plain client; (6) api.efsa.europa.eu -> JSON 404 on guessed paths, openapi.efsa.europa.eu -> connection failed; (7) data.europa.eu dataset record -> 200, license null, 0 distributions (catalogue metadata stale; publisher terms read from the publisher's own pages instead).
measurements.novelty_sweeps: 2026-11-03, three web searches: 'machine learning predicting EFSA health claim outcome opinion favourable'; '"health claims" EFSA NDA panel prediction model outcome "favourable" OR "unfavourable" study machine learning'; 'text mining predict outcome EFSA NDA opinions health claims favourable study model'. All returned EFSA's own guidance/press/statistics documents and unrelated ML-in-risk-assessment material; NO published scored study or ML-ready benchmark predicting EFSA claim-opinion outcomes was found. Prior to any ready verdict, scripts/check-novelty.py must be run with the formal verdict and the queries recorded.
measurements.not_yet_measured: Per-year claim/opinion counts and favourable rates per split window; clustered opinion counts; extraction cost of the opinions corpus; the dated worked example; the per-document journal copyright line. These are the named next probes, not estimates.

review: Strongest surviving lead of this EU/EEA session. Real user decision (food businesses invest in dossier preparation; ~20-33% favourable base rates are low enough that a naive always-negative baseline has real but bounded headroom); documented prediction instant and 5-month statutory assessment window; text-first features that suit agent/harness benchmarks; licence evidence read directly from both publishers (EFSA attribution licence; Commission CC BY 4.0). The two open risks are access-shaped, not contract-shaped: (1) whether the EFSA Journal opinion corpus is bulk-extractable (Wiley 403 to plain clients - test the supported browser before concluding, and note that a browser-only extraction is a real constraint on worker construction); (2) whether per-claim structured outcomes can be had without PDF parsing, via the FIP register API (health_claims endpoints 404 from plain clients) or the downloaded Access database.
next_action: Next probe (bounded, one session): (1) capture the real /health_claims/get_list_of_claims request the FIP SPA issues (browser network capture or the app's lazy chunks), and if reachable, measure per-claim status counts by year -> split-window counts directly; (2) else parse ndaclaims13.mdb on a worker (mdbtools) for the Art 13.1 batch panel + enumerate Art 13.5/14 opinions via the EFSA Journal; (3) test the supported browser against the Wiley 403 for one opinion PDF and record its copyright line + its Received/mandate dates as the dated worked example; (4) run scripts/check-novelty.py with the recorded queries before any ready verdict. Construction order stays: construction -> full-worker qualification -> exact-byte acceptance -> reference/model scoring.
